reply:
That “better or worse” ambivalence makes sense. Nobody coming over is a relief in the moment — no spotlight, no performative concern — but it also confirms the thing that stings: you were sitting there in open distress and the room just… kept moving. Then Debbie quits Friday, and by Monday her paperwork lands on you with zero conversation. That’s not invisible in a neutral way anymore. That’s invisible *and* convenient for them.

The money silence is the part I’d treat as the real line. Not because you owe them a confrontation, but because “nobody said one word” means the default is: you absorb the work, they keep the payroll unchanged. Silence isn’t neutral there — it’s a decision by omission.

You don’t have to solve the crying-at-desk thing and the unpaid-work thing in the same week. But the paperwork is concrete. A short, unemotional ask can be enough: “I’ve picked up Debbie’s paperwork since Monday. I want to make sure we’re aligned on scope and compensation — can we talk this week?” No apology, no over-explaining.

Do you want help drafting that, or are you still mostly in the “I can’t believe nobody said anything” stage?
